summary: A phase distribution accounts for every phase ENTRY in the sample it is printed beside: one per phase a trial is posted under, plus one for each trial posted under none. It tallies entries and not trials, so the sum exceeds the sample whenever a trial is posted under two phases — a PHASE1/PHASE2 trial belongs in both buckets and counting it once would leave the Phase 1 figure short. Phaseless trials are observational studies and count as N/A, the same answer phaseDisplay gives them for the Phase column, so the summary and the rendered rows agree. That bucket is lossy by design and Trial.Phases is where the two states stay distinguishable, empty versus ["NA"]. All four commands compute this through one helper, tallyPhases. The same per-entry rule governs the country list a report prints beside it: geo ranges over Trial.Countries, so a trial sited in three countries contributes three entries, while sponsor reads one scalar field and contributes one. Not the empty-distribution case that phase-key-always-present-on-trial-shaped-json left alone: that entry is about an empty list meaning no distribution was computed.
reason: Every tally ranged over t.Phases with no guard, so a trial with an empty Phases array entered zero buckets and vanished. Measured on a live compare: semaglutide's distribution summed to 255 against a stated sample_size of 300, tirzepatide's to 244 against 282, with no bucket accounting for the difference. The guard then existed as four byte-identical copies, only one of which any test could reach, so the rule lived in an argument that the copies matched rather than in code. Extracting tallyPhases removed the copies; report's own view was still assembled inside RunE behind a live client, so nothing could assert that report reached the helper at all.
validated_outcome: Over a twelve-trial corpus of two phaseless, eight single-phase and two two-phase trials, the distribution sums to 14 and N/A holds four. A corpus of single-phase trials cannot separate a per-trial tally from a per-entry one. buildTopicReport now takes the fetched sample and returns the briefing, so report is reachable without a client, and its own six-trial corpus carries each asserted field at zero, one and more than one — the multiplicity a single-valued fixture cannot test. Four mutations, each failing only what it should: restricting the geo loop to a trial's first country drops the country total from 8 to 5 and Canada from 3 to 1; passing total for SampleSize fails the sample assertion alone; hardcoding geo.top(8) over topN fails the bound assertion alone; negating the phaseless guard in tallyPhases fails seven tests across three files, including the new report one, which is what shows report reads the shared helper rather than a copy. compare and emerging still tally inside RunE behind a live client and remain out of reach of a test. Guarded by TestBuildTopicReportCountsPhaseEntries, TestBuildTopicReportCountsEverySite, TestBuildTopicReportCountsOneSponsorPerTrial, TestBuildTopicReportKeepsSampleSeparateFromTotals and TestBuildTopicReportRespectsTopN.
